snapshot.name: Recipe Cooking Workflow App
snapshot.description:
You are a senior React Native engineer. Scaffold a production-ready React Native (Expo) app for a “Recipe Runner” app: users save recipes and then cook them in a guided, step-by-step walkthrough mode.

GOALS
- Fast, clean scaffold with best-practice architecture.
- Focus on the core workflow: Recipe list → Recipe detail → Cook Mode (step runner) → Resume.
- Keep it minimal but extensible (no premature complexity).

TECH STACK
- Expo + TypeScript
- expo-router for navigation
- Zustand (or Redux Toolkit if you strongly prefer) for app state
- React Query (TanStack Query) for data fetching + caching
- Storage: AsyncStorage for local persistence (later can swap to SQLite/WatermelonDB)
- Form + validation: react-hook-form + zod
- UI: react-native-paper OR tamagui OR nativewind (pick one and be consistent)
- Tests: Jest + React Native Testing Library (just wiring + one sample test)

FEATURES (MVP)
1) Recipe Library
- View list of recipes (local persisted)
- Create recipe (basic fields + steps)
- Edit recipe
- Delete recipe
2) Recipe Detail
- Shows ingredients + steps summary
- “Start cooking” button
3) Cook Mode (the key)
- Full-screen step runner
- One step displayed at a time with:
  - step title
  - instruction text
  - optional “timer minutes/seconds”
  - checklist items (optional)
- Controls: Back, Next, Pause/Exit
- Persists progress (currentStepIndex, timers paused state if present) so user can resume later
- “Resume cooking” from Recipe detail if an in-progress session exists
4) Data Model (local)
- Recipe: id, title, description?, servings?, tags?, createdAt, updatedAt
- Ingredient: id, recipeId, name, quantity?, unit?, note?
- Step: id, recipeId, order, title?, instruction, timerSeconds?, checklist? (array of strings)
- CookSession: id, recipeId, startedAt, updatedAt, currentStepIndex, status (in_progress|completed|abandoned)

APP STRUCTURE REQUIREMENTS
- Use feature-based folder structure:
  - /app (routes)
  - /features/recipes (screens/components/hooks)
  - /features/cook (step runner, session logic)
  - /lib (storage, ids, date utils)
  - /store (zustand slices)
  - /types (zod schemas + TS types)
- Provide a small “repository layer” wrapping AsyncStorage so persistence is not scattered in components.
- Use Zod schemas as the source of truth for types.

DELIVERABLES
- Output the complete project file tree.
- Provide the key files’ full contents (not just snippets):
  - app/_layout.tsx, app/index.tsx
  - app/recipes/index.tsx, app/recipes/[id].tsx
  - app/recipes/new.tsx, app/recipes/[id]/edit.tsx
  - app/cook/[recipeId].tsx
  - features/cook/CookRunner.tsx
  - store/useStore.ts (or slices)
  - lib/storage.ts (AsyncStorage wrapper + migrations stub)
  - types/schemas.ts (zod)
- Include a minimal seed dataset and a “Reset demo data” dev-only button.
- Add one example unit test for the CookSession reducer/state transitions.
- Include clear run instructions: install, start, test.

CONSTRAINTS
- Don’t add auth, cloud sync, payments, or social.
- No backend; local only.
- Keep styling simple and consistent.
- Avoid overengineering; the value is the cook-mode flow + clean persistence.
